correctness.rationale: Horizontal Fourier orthogonality bounds each vertical character fiber by two. Size 2n−1 forces exactly one singleton and n−1 doubletons; singleton row ensures the missing-row kernel is removed. For the full two-layer matrix D, each doubleton contributes n²|zj−zk|² to det D and the singleton 2n. The missing-row projection onto D-column orthogonal complement has squared norm 1/(2n), so det Q=det D/(2n), v*Q^{-1}v=2n−1 and L<=1. Trace Q=(2n−1)² then U>=2n and rho>=2n. At equality Dv=2nv forces all doubletons antipodal (even m), giving Q=2n I-vv* with spectrum {1,2n^(2n−2)}. Odd m: all optimal chords yield s=sin(pi/2m), rank-one secular cubic 2n y³−(2n−1)y²−2s² y+s², plus two (n−2)-fold levels; strict interlacing gives positivity and fixed-m asymptotics. The submitted proof correctly limits odd-m condition-number optimality; determinant optimization is NOT asserted to optimize odd-m rho. Independently formed exact/complex Fourier Gram matrices for 18 small (n,m) combinations, including nontrivial odd/even m, and matched determinants and complete spectra; finite tests corroborate, not establish all n.
